### What Would You See?
- If you look in the direction of the Moon (which is **very close to the Sun**), you might see a **very faint, pale grayish glow** — but this is **not visible to the unaided eye** under normal daylight conditions.
- You would **not see the Moon as a distinct object** — it would be **too dim** and **too close to the bright Sun**.

---

### When Would You Be Able to See the Moon?
- You would be able to see the Moon with the naked eye **only after sunset**, when the sky becomes darker.
- The Moon will become visible as it **moves away from the Sun** and becomes **more illuminated** (i.e., as it goes from new moon to waxing crescent).

---

### Final Assessment:
**No, you will not be able to see the Moon with the naked eye at that time and location.** It is too faint, too close to the Sun, and the sky is too bright. You would need **binoculars or a telescope** to see it, and even then, it would be very difficult.
